The test image shows split soybean stems/roots with:
- **White/cream interior pith** (stems split lengthwise)
- **Dense black masses** at the nodes and root zone
- Fibrous root system with heavy black coating

The white pith rules out Brown Stem Rot. The black masses at nodes/roots suggest either Charcoal Rot (microsclerotia) or Sudden Death Syndrome. Let me check reference images.

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Split stems held up showing white/cream interior pith; dense black masses concentrated at nodes and root crown; heavily blackened fibrous root system
- **Charcoal Rot reference**: Shows gray/charcoal discoloration on lower stems from microsclerotia; split stems confirm black speckling
- **SDS reference**: Shows white pith + leaf interveinal chlorosis/necrosis + root rot, but the root darkening pattern looks different
- **SCN reference**: Shows individual dark cysts on fine roots — not the dense clumped masses seen here

**Key reasoning**: The test image shows the classic Charcoal Rot presentation — stems split to reveal the root/lower stem area coated with **dense black microsclerotia**, giving that charcoal-like appearance. The concentration at node/root crown regions and the heavy black coating on the taproot and laterals matches the description: *"numerous tiny, black fungal structures called microsclerotia scattered throughout the pith and on the surface of taproots and lower stems."* The pith appearing white/cream is consistent with Charcoal Rot (vs. Brown Stem Rot which shows brown pith discoloration).
